PC-OTH-016.question: A producer convinces a client to replace an existing policy by misrepresenting the current coverage. This unethical practice is called:
PC-OTH-016.explanation: Twisting is inducing replacement through misrepresentation, an unfair practice under s. 626.9541. Rebating is giving back part of the commission, which Florida allows only under a filed, uniformly applied schedule (s. 626.572), and coercion is forcing a purchase, such as tying insurance to a loan.

PC-AUTO-017.explanation: Underinsured coverage applies when the at-fault driver has liability insurance but not enough to pay the damages. In Florida, s. 627.727(3)(b) treats a vehicle whose bodily injury limits are less than the injured person's total damages as uninsured, so UM coverage pays the gap. A driver with no insurance at all is plain UM.

PC-AUTO-016.explanation: A vehicle is uninsured when there is no liability policy, the insurer denies coverage or is insolvent, or it is a hit-and-run vehicle. Florida (s. 627.727(3)) also treats a vehicle as uninsured when its bodily injury limits are less than the injured person's total damages. A liability insurer that pays the damages in full leaves no UM claim.

PC-AUTO-015.explanation: UM pays bodily injury damages the insured is legally entitled to recover from an at-fault driver who has no liability insurance or cannot be identified. In Florida, UM under s. 627.727 covers bodily injury only; damage to the car is a collision claim.

PC-AUTO-030.explanation: After 60 days the PAP lets the insurer cancel only for nonpayment of premium, a suspended or revoked license, or material misrepresentation. Florida's s. 627.728 uses the same grounds for private passenger auto, with 45 days' notice, or 10 days for nonpayment.

PC-POL-024.explanation: When the insurer cancels, the insured receives the full unearned portion in proportion to time remaining. When the insured cancels, a short rate penalty may apply, but Florida limits it: auto insurers may keep no more than 10 percent of unearned premium (s. 627.7283), and other property and casualty short rate tables generally must return at least 90 percent of the pro rata amount.

PC-POL-023.optionC: Can be paid even if the insured's claim is denied
PC-POL-023.explanation: The mortgagee has rights independent of the insured, so a denial for the insured's own acts, such as fraud or neglect, does not void the lender's protection. The loss must still be covered, and the mortgagee is paid only up to its interest in the property.
